finding: With the qemu ADT profile the kernel reaches PE_init_iokit and then the bootstrap thread blocks in ml_wait_max_cpus() on max_cpus_lock while the boot CPU idles. The value read at _max_cpus_initialized (2) is not a CPU count: in XNU it is MAX_CPUS_WAIT, the waiter's own state. The loop exits only when ml_set_max_cpus() sets MAX_CPUS_SET, and the caller of that is IOCPUInterruptController in iokit/Kernel/IOCPU.cpp -- so the wait is for the platform interrupt controller to register. That never happens because ArmCpu's GIC bring-up stops inside prepareDistributor(): ArmCpu::start ran, gicv2::Controller::prepareDistributor ran, prepareLocal never did (the || in prepareGic short-circuits on the first false), so enableLocal, enableGic and initCPU never run, no CPU interrupt source exists, and no IRQ or FIQ is ever delivered.
not_proven: which condition inside prepareDistributor() returns false (its fail/verify helpers are inlined in the kernel build, so no symbol shows it)
XNU entry or iOS userland on a handset
anything about the eMMC, display or GPU on real hardware
